items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: he's sort of like Cuba Kewpie Bennett.

ctx.x: so consequently he could write, (unintelligible) That was up Billy's alley. So they were playing this fast two/four. Billy always sit down (unintelligible) and crossed his legs and (unintelligible) play like nothing ever happened. So when he got to these chords, Roy was running, you know, and when Billy got to it, everybody sat there and listened. He ran over all those chords, didn't miss no chords and (unintelligible) run the music. Where in the hell did that guy come from? I said, he's been in New York before.…
Said, what? I said, sure. So, cheese and crackers, mister, he's sort of like Cuba Kewpie Bennett. I said (unintelligible).
